description:
Research a public repository or package to answer a question with sources. Omit target and thread_id to identify the target from the question. If Research returns candidates, retry with the one matching the question's project as target. Supply at most one of target or thread_id. Continue a prior thread by its returned thread_id. Follow-ups can change project, version, or topic; state changes in the question. Returns a verified answer that always includes its sources, so ask the question directly without requesting citations, an overview or a source-cited answer. Cite those sources directly; read one only when the answer lacks a detail you need. Sources default to MCP read calls; request source_format=url for original upstream URLs.

Before using this tool, call `quick_start` once per session unless the `githits-mcp` skill is loaded.

format.description: Omit `format` to use token-efficient text when the model reads the result or chooses follow-up tools. Set `json` only when code consumes the raw response instead of the model, or a required field is absent from text.

question.description: One research question to answer from indexed public evidence, asked directly; sources are always included. Do not include credentials, personal data, private code, or proprietary content.

source_format.description: Source pointer format. `mcp` returns read calls for opening a source only when needed; `url` returns original upstream HTTP URLs.

target.description: Optional canonical open-source package or repository target, such as npm:express or github:expressjs/express. Never a docs site (site:): research covers the project's code and docs. Omit target and thread_id to identify the target from the question.

thread_id.description: Thread UUID returned by an earlier research call. Cannot be combined with target. Reuse it for follow-ups; name a new project or version in the question to change scope.

name: research
